newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: GOLF-LANGER WINS CZECH OPEN, GARRIDO RYDER CUP PLACE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LANGER WINS CZECH OPEN, GARRIDO RYDER CUP PLACE.

text.p: Bernhard Langer won the Czech Open with a magnificent final round 63 on Sunday.
He started the final round four strokes behind leader Ignacio Garrido and rocketed to the title by a stunning four-shot margin.

Garrido had to settle for joint second place with Sweden's Niclas Fasth after fading to a 71 after three rounds in the mid-60s but assured himself of a place in Europe's Ryder Cup team to meet the Americans next month.
The young Spaniard followed in his father Antonio's footsteps by making the line-up for Valderrama -- the only father and son to achieve the honour after Britain's Percy and Peter Alliss.
Langer took his third European title of the year and 37th of his 21-year career with a closing eight-under-par round to follow his 64 of Saturday.
He finished with a 20-under total of 264 as he ran up 15 birdies for the two rounds without dropping a shot.
Langer collected $211,000 to go second in Europe's order of merit behind Ian Woosnam.
A bogey on the 17th cost Garrido second place outright but the Madrid player moved to sixth in the Ryder Cup points table, comfortably among the leading 10 automatic qualifying places.
Garrido began the final round a stroke ahead of compatriot Miguel Angel Jimenez, while Fasth came through the field with a 66.
Jimenez took the lead from Garrido early on but Langer passed him with a birdie on the 12th and moved up a gear in a similar finish to his closing and triumphant 63 at the Italian Open.
"I knew I had to do something special to win," said the German, who proved himself in good shape on the eve of the final major, the U.S. PGA championship.
"I thought I might need 64 or 65 so this was a nice surprise. It will be a different challenge for the U.S. PGA but I hope my game stays in similar shape."

Garrido's inclusion in the Ryder Cup team alongside Langer, who was already assured a place before his latest victory, was welcomed by the German, who finished fourth behind the Spaniard in the German Open recently.
"The team's working out to be a good mixture of experience and youth. Now Ignacio has broken through I am sure he is going to be a great asset," added Langer.
